claim_scope: This package certifies an accounting ledger and its exact price: the whole-bank volume condition, the retained row identity with the stock falling by the bank count, both complex paid moments with the adjacent 10^-18 grid point excluded, the unchanged 47-constraint assembly at the rung-2 budget with its adjacent point rejected, and an independent replica of the same ledger in PR208's pricing convention. The rung is NOT constructed: C1 has no precedent in the pins and C5 has no inventory. The kappa is therefore a priced, exactly certified target conditional on C1-C5 and on #219's inherited R1-R4, and it is not a completed finite witness or an unconditional multiplication theorem in any case.

obligations.name: inventory and provenance of the rank-11 family
obligations.statement: Enumerate the rank-11 items: for each of the 1,062 per-vertex children of the complex ledger's bin 11, the frame/chain occurrence it comes from, with a checked bijection onto the 3,186 three-copy occurrences and a proof that no other bin is touched. The pins contain no such inventory; the only occurrence inventory they hold is #219's bit-side inputs/absorbed-occurrences.json for the rank-22 bin, which is what makes #219's R1 a closed checklist.

obligations.name: rank-16 family inventory on the complex word
obligations.reference_precedent: PR219 references/pr219-run1/inputs/absorbed-occurrences.json (rank-22 provenance), which this family has no counterpart of.
obligations.statement: Enumerate the complex word's rank-16 child family: its 264 occurrences per vertex (792 over the three copies), their frame or chain identity, a bijection onto the 192 three-copy blocks the absorption of rung 3 needs, and a proof that no other bin of the ledger moves. Nothing in the pins enumerates this family, exactly as nothing enumerates the rank-11 family of PR224 or the rank-22 bin of PR219's bit-side absorption, whose inventory (inputs/absorbed-occurrences.json) is what made that rung a closed checklist.
obligations.why_it_is_the_blocker: A rung that cannot name its items cannot be built: the item-to-block map of C1 has no starting inventory for this family, so its absorption is priced but not instantiated.

obligations.name: rank-20 family inventory on the complex word
obligations.statement: The same enumeration for the rank-20 family: 66 occurrences per vertex (198 over the three copies) onto the 60 three-copy blocks of rung 4, with the same no-other-bin-moves proof.
obligations.why_it_is_the_blocker: Same gap as C6, one rung further; it is the last family of the ledger that satisfies the whole-bank volume condition.

obligations.name: mixed tiling of the width-66 bank for ranks 16 and 20
obligations.reference_precedent: PR219 references/pr219-run1/schedule.py (width-72 tilings over {4, 24, 22}); research/coordinated-frames-and-entrance-banks BANK-PROOF-PR200.md (18 four-coordinate cores or 3 24-coordinate cores fill a width-72 bank).
obligations.statement: Rank 11 divides the bank width (66 = 6 x 11) and needed no mixture, but 66 = 4 x 16 + 2 and 66 = 3 x 20 + 6: the rank-16 and rank-20 blocks cannot tile a 66-wide bank on their own, so their banks must mix block sizes. The obligation is to enumerate the admissible tilings of width 66 over the families the complex word actually offers, choose one per bank, and show that the chosen pattern realises exactly 264 rank-16 and 66 rank-20 children per vertex -- i.e. that every absorbed item lands in some block and no block is left half-used.
obligations.why_it_is_the_blocker: It is the same obligation PR219 carries as R1 for the bit word (admissible tilings of width 72 over families {4, 24, 22}), but with no analogous enumeration to inherit: the bit word's bank pattern is pinned in the bank proof, the complex word has none.

status: OPEN obligations for rungs 3 and 4. verify.py certifies the accounting (whole-bank volumes, retained row identities, stock drops equal to the bank counts, both paid moments on the 10^-18 grid, the two 47-constraint assemblies and the exclusion of the adjacent grid points) and the exact prices; it discharges none of these items.

why_rung_3_and_4.consequence: the accounting ladder on the complex word terminates at rung 4; going higher needs a different bank width, a different ledger (a new supplier), or a mixed tiling that reopens the volume condition.

numbers.remaining_families: every one of the 17 families left after rungs 2-4 has a volume that is not a whole number of width-66 banks

why_rung_3_and_4.statement: Rung 2 (PR224) absorbs the complex word's rank-11 family and lands on the complex branch's new ceiling, so the only way up is to raise the complex coarse saving again. Exactly two further families of that ledger satisfy the whole-bank volume condition -- rank 16 and rank 20 -- and after them no family does.
